title: PI-KNN: k-nearest neighbors on the π circle with depth weighting

the_thesis.concept: every organism has a pi_pos — a position on the unit circle from the binary chain hash. KNN asks: who are your NEIGHBORS on π? do taxonomic neighbors match π-neighbors?
the_thesis.pi_distance: angular distance on the unit circle. wraps around: 0.99 and 0.01 are 0.02 apart, not 0.98.
the_thesis.pi_depth: depth in the tree of life (domain=1, kingdom=2, phylum=3, genus=4, species=5, organism=6). deeper = more specific = "heavier" in KNN weighting.
the_thesis.knn: k-nearest neighbors: find the k closest organisms on π. if your neighbors share your kingdom/genus, π encodes taxonomy. if they DON'T, π found something taxonomy missed.
the_thesis.the_question: does the math (π hash) agree with the biology (taxonomy)? where it agrees = confirmation. where it disagrees = DISCOVERY.

pi_clusters.concept: organisms within 0.025 (9°) of each other on π form natural clusters

surprises.concept: organisms that are close on π but distant in taxonomy — the π-hash found convergences that naming missed

knn_accuracy.concept: if we predict kingdom/genus from π-neighbors alone, how accurate is the hash?
knn_accuracy.interpretation: k=3: kingdom=85.6%, genus=20.0%. k=5: kingdom=88.7%, genus=22.0%. k=7: kingdom=87.1%, genus=20.9%. HIGH kingdom coherence — π DOES encode taxonomy.

measurement_connection.knn_uses_ratio_scale: pi_distance is RATIO scale — true zero (0 = same position), meaningful ratios (0.02 is twice as close as 0.04)
measurement_connection.depth_is_ordinal: tree depth is ORDINAL — domain < kingdom < phylum < genus < species. deeper IS more specific but "twice as deep" is undefined.
measurement_connection.combined: pi_depth_distance = angular × (1 + 1/depth). this MIXES ratio (angular) with ordinal (depth). the mix IS the machine learning trick — combining scales to get a better distance metric.
measurement_connection.this_is_ml: KNN is the simplest ML algorithm. it has ONE assumption: things that are CLOSE are SIMILAR. we test that assumption on the π circle.
